newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's D'Onofrio plans new $13 mln plant.
newsitem.headline: Peru's D'Onofrio plans new $13 mln plant.

text.p: Peruvian ice cream maker D'Onofrio, a blue chip on the Lima bolsa, plans to invest up to $13 million on a new production plant in a bid to satisfy local demand and expand into markets abroad, a company official said Wednesday.
D'Onofrio hopes the plant will come on-line early next year, marketing manager Harold Mongrut said in an interview.

He did not give details on the size of the new plant but said the increased production would help D'Onofrio defend its 90 percent market share in Peru and gain up to a 10 percent market share in neighboring Bolivia and Chile, Mongrut said.

While D'Onofrio also plans to enter two more neighboring markets -- Ecuador and Colombia -- its bottom-line goal is to keep at bay Switzerland's Nestle and Bresler & Reiner Inc, which are both agressively trying to enter the Peruvian market, he said.
Bresler is owned by the Anglo-Dutch firm Unilver.
Magrut added: "This summer (December to March) we responded convincingly. The ice cream market is ours and we will fight for our 90 percent to the last."
